extracted.intended_audience: researchers and clinicians designing or evaluating measurement instruments and reliability/validation studies (psychometricians, instrument developers, clinical researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical findings about assessing and reporting inter-rater and intra-rater reliability and validity of measurement instruments across clinical and field settings; includes recommended metrics, training procedures, thresholds, and validation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability (observed agreement and kappa coefficient)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare agreement between multiple raters using observed agreement and kappa coefficient (e.g., Fleiss' kappa) to quantify consistency across raters for items and instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percent/observed agreement together with kappa; studies reported substantial inter-rater agreement across methods and used >70% of items with at least substantial agreement as evidence of acceptable inter-rater reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-rater reliability (observed agreement and kappa coefficient)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the same rater produces consistent scores across occasions using observed agreement and kappa statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report intra-rater observed agreement and kappa; e.g., intra-rater agreement comparing methods resulted in observed agreement >75% for most items in cited studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of kappa statistics (Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, weighted/quadratic kappa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply appropriate kappa variant for categorical data: Cohen's kappa for pairwise raters, Fleiss' kappa for multiple raters, weighted/quadratic kappa for ordered categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which kappa is used and present values with interpretation; several studies reported Kw (Fleiss-Cohen weights), quadratic-weighted kappa, and used kappa ranges to judge item-level agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) for continuous/ordinal scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICC to quantify agreement for continuous or scaled measurements (e.g., total scores, window-ad counts, dynamometry readings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ICC with confidence intervals; ICC was used for window observations, HHD, MMT total scores and to categorize levels of agreement (see acceptable thresholds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent agreement and prevalence-adjusted bias-adjusted kappa (PABAK)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report raw percent agreement and consider prevalence/bias effects by reporting PABAK or adjusted kappa when item prevalence is extreme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-store items showed many with 100% agreement; PABAK indicated excellent agreement (≥0.90) except where prevalence or bias affected kappa (examples: aisle width).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specified thresholds for acceptable reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify measures as acceptable or not using cutoffs such as ICC≥0.75, percent agreement≥80%, kappa≥0.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WorkWell Systems systematic review explicitly categorised ICC≥0.75, percentages of agreement≥80%, and kappa≥0.60 as acceptable; use consistent, justified thresholds when judging reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report measurement error: SEM, SDC, and 95% confidence intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the standard error of measurement (SEM), smallest detectable change (SDC), and 95% CI ranges for scores to quantify absolute measurement error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMAT reported SEM and 95% CI range not exceeding 2 points; HHD and other strength measures reported SEM% and SDC% to contextualize ICC results. Include these to interpret clinical meaningfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha) and dimensionality (factor analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess internal consistency with Cronbach's alpha and evaluate construct dimensionality using factor analysis/community values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report alpha with CIs; e.g., AMSTAR translation reported Cronbach's alpha 0.91 and factor analysis supported unidimensionality. Use item-level statistics to support scale structure claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic accuracy and validity (sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, association with gold standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: For instruments intended to identify clinical conditions, report sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and compare to a gold standard (e.g., MRI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pain drawing study reported high sensitivity (93%) but low specificity (19%) and poor agreement with clinical assessment (kappa=0.11). Report both agreement and diagnostic accuracy measures to understand utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized rater training to improve reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide and describe rater training (e.g., single self-directed electronic module, 30-minute briefing with practice, or 1.5-hour workshop) prior to scoring to reduce rater variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several studies found that minimal, standardized training enabled acceptable inter-rater reliability; RAMP study found training, not prior experience, minimized differences. Document training content, duration, and practice cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of scoring scale: categorical versus continuous
rubrics_metrics.description: Select an appropriate scoring scale (e.g., 3-point categorical vs visual analogue continuous) and assess whether scale choice affects reliability and predictive utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reflex/injury scoring (RAMP), authors recommended a 3-point categorical scale over a continuous tVAS because the continuous scale did not improve model fit and categorical scores produced robust relationships with survival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-cultural translation and validation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: For instrument translation: use parallel back-translation, expert committee review(s), clarity/ambiguity ratings by target users, pilot rating of real reviews/documents, and statistical reliability/validity testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: French-Canadian AMSTAR used a modified Vallerand approach: parallel back-translation, two expert committees, clarity ratings by future professionals, and final adjustments; then measure ICC/kappa/Cronbach's alpha and factor structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item analysis: degree of difficulty and discriminative validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform item-level analyses to assess item difficulty and discriminative validity to confirm items function as intended within the instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Q-DIO study used item analyses to confirm fulfilment of criteria for degree of difficulty and discriminative validity; include these analyses when validating scales and reporting problematic items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report multiple agreement coefficients (e.g., Gwet's AC1, Fleiss' kappa) when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing concordance, consider reporting different agreement statistics (Gwet's AC1, Fleiss' kappa, Cohen's kappa) to address methodological limitations of any single coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obstetric claims study reported absolute agreement, Fleiss' kappa and Gwet's AC1; using multiple indices can clarify agreement especially when kappa paradoxes or prevalence effects are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define explicit categorical scoring labels and numeric codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear, operationalized category definitions (e.g., pain index: absence=0, slight=1, marked=2) so raters have unambiguous criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neck Reflex Points study explicitly defined PI categories; clear category definitions help achieve higher PA and kappa and facilitate training and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report per-item/component reliability and total score reliability; identify problematic components
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide reliability metrics at both the item/component level and the aggregate/total score level, and discuss components with low agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test of Gross Motor Development-2 showed excellent total ICC but some skill components had lower agreement; recommend revising or clarifying problematic components to improve reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess inter-method agreement (comparing measurement modalities)
rubrics_metrics.description: When instruments have multiple data-collection methods (e.g., on-site sketch vs digital photo, street-level vs parcel-level, virtual vs in-person), assess inter-method agreement in addition to inter-rater agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Food Retail Outlet Survey Tool and SSO studies compared inter-method and inter-rater agreements; report intraclass correlation coefficients for method comparisons and note method-specific discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting quality, risk of bias, and adherence to reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and report the quality of study reporting and potential for bias; follow established reporting guidelines for reliability and validity studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICH classification systems review noted variable reporting quality and potential bias and recommended future studies follow recently published reporting guidelines; include methods, rater expertise, blinding, sampling, and statistical approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling and study design considerations for reliability studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate sampling (random or stratified where relevant), adequate numbers of raters and cases, and representative settings to support generalizability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Food stores were randomly selected from eligible lists and ground-truthed; many reliability studies used experienced raters in specialist centers — explicitly report sampling frame and discuss generalizability limitations.
